title: X-15
note: North American X-15, the basic airplane (not the X-15A-2). Frame: x forward (nose tip at the front), y left, z up; fuselage centreline on z = 0; gear up, lower (ventral) fin on, as in the three-view drawings. Feet from the sources are converted at 0.3048 m/ft. No reference 3D model exists (see reference_model): layout and shapes come from the dimensioned three-view drawings in refs/x15/ and Table I of NASA TN D-3343.

reference_model.note: None. NASA 3D Resources has no X-15 (whole repository tree searched, 2026-10-27; it has the X-57). The Smithsonian record's 57 media items are all images, and an Open Access search for 3D media returned nothing. Layout comes from the three-view drawings instead (refs/x15/three-view-1966.png, nasa_tnd3343 Fig. 1; three-view-1960.png, nasa_tmx430 Fig. 1).

open_questions: Length: 49.5 ft (1966 basic airplane, blunt nose) vs 50.75 ft (1960 airplane, pointed nose, excluding the nose boom) vs the museum's 1554.5 cm (51 ft, ball nose). The spec uses 49.5 ft with the ball nose, matching the museum airframe's nose (photo NASM2018-10035). The museum figure is 0.46 m longer and its method isn't stated.
Which X-15 and markings: the museum's X-15 #1 (tail 56-6670, "U.S. AIR FORCE", NASA tail band) is the proposal.
Gear up (in flight, as the drawings) or down (skids and nose wheel) and the lower fin on or off. The spec assumes up and on.

Not in any source read: wing position along the fuselage, fuselage cross-sections, side-fairing length and width, nose and canopy shape, engine nozzle exit size, skid and nose-gear positions. They would be measured from the 1966 three-view (scaled by its 49.5 ft length) and labelled "estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png". Next documents to try: NASA TN D-1057 (Matranga), which Jenkins cites.
Leading-edge sweep is derived from the quarter-chord sweep and the chords (geometry), not quoted.
Engine nozzle: not modelled. Jenkins (ch. 4) gives the XLR99 nozzle as a 20-degree cone with a 9.8:1 expansion ratio, but no exit diameter was found, and no museum photo shows the base.
Wingtip pods: left off (David's call). They are not in the 1966 three-view; Jenkins (ch. 8) gives them as 8 in by 58 in, fitted to X-15-1 from October 1964.

from_drawing.scale_note: At the 49.5 ft scale the drawn fuselage matches Table I both ways (depth 4.67, width across the fairings 7.18 vs 7.33), but the wings, tails and fins are drawn about 10% short in span (wing 20.5 vs the labelled 22.4, horizontal tail 16.2 vs 18.1, fin tip to fin tip 11.8 vs 13.1). So spans and chords come from Table I; the drawing gives positions along the length and the fuselage shape. x is aft from the nose tip, z up from the fuselage's mid-depth at its deepest section, y left.

fuselage.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px); top view for half_width (the body edge inside the side fairings from x 14), side view for top and bottom. Top under the canopy is interpolated; aft of x 30 the drawn top line has faded and is held at the forward value, which also puts the fin roots 4.69 ft apart as Table I's 13.1 - 4.58 - 3.83 requires.

side_fairings.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px); top view outline (scaled up 2% so the widest station gives Table I's 7.33 ft), side view lozenge. The drawn fairings start in a rounded nose at x 12.9 and end at x 48.8. The fillet (0.7 ft, the smooth-union blend between body and fairing) and the body's width inside the fairings (0.75 of the plan's inner line, narrowing from where the fairings start to x 20) are estimated from the front view, whose sides are concave between the fairings and the canopy and under the belly. The fairing section is a superellipse of exponent 1.5 (diamond-like, its outer edge sharp at wing level), estimated from the same view. The first three half-widths are reduced by up to 0.1 ft so the fairings grow out of the body without a nub; they end in a step at x 48.8, as drawn.

canopy.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px), measured to the middle of the drawn lines. Side view: the hood runs from its front corner at (6.81, 1.81) up a straight windscreen slope to the top at (8.71, 2.69), along the top to the aft frame at x 11.74 (z 2.64), and back along the sill, which drops to z 1.1 by x 8; the aft fairing runs from the frame down to the spine (2.39 at x 14.4) and ends at x 17.2. Top view: the frame (the hood's base) is a rounded rectangle 2.9 ft wide from x 6.8; above it the windscreen is a V: each pane's lower edge (z 1.81 in the side view) runs from 0.39 ft off the centreline at x 7.43 to 1.30 at x 10.5, its upper edge (z 2.35) from 0.32 at x 8.53 to 0.93 at x 10.57; the aft fairing tapers from 1.1 at the frame to a point at x 17.2. Each section is a polyline through those widths, with a rounded roof (a quarter ellipse, estimated from photo NASM2018-10035) from the upper level to the top. The top, 2.69, makes the depth over the canopy 5.09 ft with the 2.40 ft bottom: 2.4% over Table I's 4.97. To join the parts smoothly (estimated): the widths at the frame are eased to the fairing's (1.0 at the windows' upper edge), the upper level starts where the windscreen slope passes z 2.35 (x 7.96), the fairing's roof starts at 2.35 at the frame and at 2.0 by x 13, and the hood's front ends in a point at x 6.7. Revised from photos NASM-SI-2007-12573, -12578, NASM-SI-2008-5563 and -5565 (nasm_x15) and the user's photo of the canopy from above: a round tube whose front is a sharp V of two flat faces, one window on each: arch.half_width is the hood base in the top view (0.5 ft at x 6.81, 0.73 at 7.0, 0.97 at 7.2, 1.08 at 7.4, 1.15 at 8.0, mean of both sides) up to the front view's widest arch, 1.2 ft; the front view's arch fits a half-ellipse 1.2 ft wide from z_shoulder 2.0 to the top (half-widths 1.05, 0.79, 0.63 drawn at z 2.3, 2.5, 2.6; the fit gives 1.08, 0.84, 0.62). The faces meet at the side view's top line from (6.81, 1.83) to (8.71, 2.69); windscreen_plan_tan (each face's sideways run per foot aft, 0.34) is the top view's V line, from the centreline at x 7.45 to 0.875 ft at x 10.0 (0.43, 0.58, 0.73 at x 8.5, 9.0, 9.5). Aft of the frame the fairing keeps the hood's arch, narrowing in proportion to the drawn fairing_half_width (photos NASM-SI-2007-12573 and NASM-SI-2008-5563 show the roof running smoothly back into it).

wing.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px); tip leading edge (both tips 31.9-32.1; tip chord 3.15 drawn vs 2.98), wing mid-plane from the edge-on lens in the side view. With Table I's chords, span and 25.64 deg sweep this puts the root leading edge at x 23.66; the drawn leading edge at x 28 lies 0.3 ft from that line.

horizontal_tail.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px); tip leading edge (tip chord 2.0 drawn vs 2.11), and the side view's upper edge where the tail leaves the side fairing (z -0.58, half-width 3.6).

upper_vertical_tail.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px); side view, the trailing edge is vertical at x 48.45 (drawn tip chord 7.62 vs Table I 7.56).

lower_vertical_tail.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px); side view, vertical trailing edge at x 48.3.

ball_nose.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png (TN D-3343 Fig. 1, rendered at 400 dpi), scaled by its 49.5 ft length (1695 px); side view, nose tip at z 0.44 and the section centre at x 1.4 at 0.39. Shape (round front, cone back to the base) estimated from the same drawing; length and base diameter are Jenkins's.

canopy_windows.source: nasa_tnd3343, Fig. 1 p.20: estimated from refs/x15/three-view-1966.png, scaled by its 49.5 ft length: the side view draws each window as a trapezoid from x 7.69 to 10.17 ft (the top view ends them at 10.5-10.57; the mean, 10.35, is used) between z 1.81 and 2.35, its front edge sloping from (7.69, 1.86) to (8.71, 2.35); the top view draws the two windows meeting near the centreline at the front. The window is that outline projected sideways onto the canopy. Centre post half-width estimated from photo NASM2018-10035 (front view, a narrow post between the two panes).

yellow_band.source: nasm_x15, photos NASM2018-10035 and -10037: a straight line parallel to the fuselage splits the fixed fin from the moving upper part; nasa_tnd3343 Fig. 1 p.20 draws that split 38% of the way up the fin (z 3.27 ft over a root at 1.58 and tip at 6.05). Photo NASM-SI-2007-12585: the moving part is black with a yellow stripe across it (NASA in black, thin black lines along its edges); the stripe is painted (livery fin_stripe).

round_nose.source: nasm_x15, photo NASM2018-10038: the cone behind the ball nose is round in section; its radius is taken as the mean of the drawn half-width and half-depth, starting at the ball nose's 13.75 in base (jenkins_sp2007) and blending into the drawn sections between x 3.5 and 10 ft (estimated).

ball_nose_shape.source: nasm_x15, photo NASM2018-10038: the sphere sits in a lip slightly wider than itself (about 8%, estimated), which starts half a sphere diameter behind the tip, so a hemisphere stands out of it (David's call, 2026-10-28: the sphere protruded too far at three quarters of a diameter); from there a straight cone runs to the 13.75 in base. In the photo the sphere is about half the base's width (6.5/13.75 = 0.47) and the cone ends at the riveted frame ahead of the two-hole panel, so the bare metal is the sensor only.

window_frame.source: nasm_x15, photos NASM2018-10035 and -10039: each window pane sits in a raised frame round its whole outline, with the two front frames meeting at the centre post; the frame is about a sixth of the window's height wide (estimated; the window is 0.54 ft tall in nasa_tnd3343 Fig. 1) and stands slightly proud of the hood (height estimated)

canopy_top.source: nasm_x15, photos NASM-SI-2008-5558 and NASM-SI-2007-12578. 5558 (the whole aircraft from ahead and above, the hood outlined against the black background): a pinhole camera fitted to the aircraft's outline (hood excluded; 1 - IoU 0.085) puts the body and spine on the photo's outline, while the hood's outline, which in that view is its cross-section near the aft frame (x 11-12), runs 0.37-0.42 ft above the model's at the roof and within 0.1 ft at the sides below z 2.4. So the roof is the drawn top line (from_drawing.canopy.top) raised 0.38 ft, the windscreen ridge keeps the drawn slope from the front corner (6.81, 1.83) until it meets the raised roof. From the roof's end (11.74, 3.02) to the spine (17.2, 2.28) the line is one S-curve, level at both ends (photos 12578 and 5563: the hood's back runs smoothly into the fuselage); it passes within 0.05 ft of the photo-fitted heights at x 12.5, 15.5 and 16.5 (2.97, 2.45, 2.35) and 0.04 ft above 13.5 (2.80). The windscreen faces are flat: the ridge runs straight at the drawn slope up to the roof (user's review of the photos). The raised roof gives a depth of 4.75 ft at the canopy station (Table I: maximum depth over canopy 4.97; nasa_tmx430 Fig. 1, refs/x15/three-view-1960.png, draws about 4.8 there at its own scale).

canopy_window.source: nasm_x15, photo NASM-SI-2008-5558 (the left window from ahead and above): the glass outline's corners, read at 5x zoom (pixels (551,352), (657,354), (683,409), (548,415), (537,389) and (615,412) on the bottom edge), each cast onto the model hood (from_photos.canopy_top) through the camera fitted to the aircraft's outline (see canopy_top), and kept as (x, z): front bottom (8.20, 2.13), front (8.30, 2.34), top front (8.91, 2.63), top rear (11.12, 2.57), bottom rear (10.58, 2.10), bottom (9.29, 2.12). The glass mostly lies on the flat front face. This replaces from_drawing.canopy_windows, whose window is 0.3 ft lower and smaller; the corners shift with the hood shape they are cast onto (estimated ±0.05 ft).

speed_brake_plate.source: nasm_x15, photo NASM-SI-2008-5570 (straight from behind, camera fitted, 5.5 px landmark rms): the upper fin's speed brakes are two plates with an open slot between them back to the fixed fin (actuator inside); each plate's rear edge is about 14 px against the fin box's 245 px (0.49 m) just above, so about 3 cm. Photos NASM-SI-2007-12585 and -12586 show the same slot from the side.

nozzle.source: nasm_x15, photo NASM-SI-2008-5570 (straight from behind, camera fitted, 5.5 px landmark rms; 534 px per m at the base): along the row through the axis the bare plate starts 0.48 m out, the red rim sits at 0.322 m on both sides. Depth 1.0 m is an estimate (not measured); the throat radius follows from it: the dark hole deep inside is 27 px across its radius, which at 1.0 m behind the base, seen from the fitted camera 3.64 m aft, is 0.065 m.

fairing_end_ribs.source: nasm_x15, photo NASM-SI-2008-5570 flattened onto the fairing end plane (x 0.213 m) at 300 px/m through its fitted camera: the ribs repeat every 9 px (autocorrelation of brightness down the right-hand face), so 3 cm; each bright rib is about a third of that. How far they stand out (8 mm) is estimated.

livery.source: nasm_x15. Each marking is a sheet on the skin (world m: its middle, the way it is looked at, its top; width x height along the skin), placed by casting its corners in a museum photo onto the model through that photo's fitted camera; masks are the photo flattened onto the sheet, paint thresholded against the local background. Fitted cameras: refs/x15/cameras/.

markings.name: us_air_force
markings.source: nasm_x15. Position: the letters' corners in photo NASM-SI-2008-5559, pixels (1003,652), (998,592), (1128,498), (1140,548), cast onto the top face of the left side fairing (x 5.50 to 8.52 m). Masks: photo NASM-SI-2007-12575 (landmark fit, 11.7 px rms), seam above the letters cut away. Right side: the mirror image (photo NASM-SI-2008-5559 shows it there).

markings.name: fin_stripe
markings.source: nasm_x15. Photo NASM-SI-2007-12585 (fin, left side), camera fitted to six fin-box corners (7.6 px rms), flattened onto the fin's side at 600 px/m; yellow traced by colour saturation, so the letters and edge lines stay black skin. Ahead of the N the stripe's cross-section is carried to the leading edge. Right side: the mirror image. Right side: the stripe mirrored, NASA still reading forwards at its mirrored place (as the left side's, photo NASM-SI-2008-5559 shows NASA there).

markings.name: fin_number
markings.source: nasm_x15. 66670 from photo NASM-SI-2007-12585, same fitted camera, flattened onto the fixed fin below the moving part. Right side: the mirror image. Right side: the digits at their mirrored place, behind the leading edge as on the left.

markings.name: usaf_lower_left
markings.source: nasm_x15. Photo NASM-SI-2008-5567 (underside from behind), camera fitted to eight corners (horizontal tail tips, wing tips at the trailing edge, fin top; 7.9 px rms), flattened onto the wing's underside at 400 px/m; paint thresholded, chips closed. Laid square to the fuselage (David, 2026-10-28): USAF turned back 12 deg (its stems lean 12.3 and 11.6 deg, its row 12.4 deg), the insignia 8.9 deg (its bars' measured angle). The photo's edge cuts the tops of the U and S: the U's strokes are carried up to the A's and F's full height, the S's top is its bottom turned (a block S is point-symmetric).

markings.name: star_lower_right
markings.source: nasm_x15. Photo NASM-SI-2008-5567 (underside from behind), camera fitted to eight corners (horizontal tail tips, wing tips at the trailing edge, fin top; 7.9 px rms), flattened onto the wing's underside at 400 px/m; paint thresholded, chips closed. Laid square to the fuselage (David, 2026-10-28): USAF turned back 12 deg (its stems lean 12.3 and 11.6 deg, its row 12.4 deg), the insignia 8.9 deg (its bars' measured angle). The photo's edge cuts the tops of the U and S: the U's strokes are carried up to the A's and F's full height, the S's top is its bottom turned (a block S is point-symmetric).

markings.name: usaf_upper_right
markings.source: nasm_x15. Same mask as usaf_lower_left, at its mirror place on top of the right wing: photo NASM-SI-2007-12575 (overhead, fitted camera) shows USAF there, inboard end at y -1.35 m as in the underside photo (+1.35 m).

markings.name: star_upper_left
markings.source: nasm_x15. Same mask as star_lower_right, at its mirror place on top of the left wing (photos NASM-SI-2008-5559 and -5560 show the star there).

markings.name: nose_dart
markings.source: nasm_x15. Drawn from points read off two photos flattened onto the left side of the nose: front tip from NASM-SI-2008-5559 (fitted camera), aft tips, notch and circle from NASM-SI-2007-12578 (camera fitted to seven points cast from 5559: RESCUE box corners and dart tips, 24 px rms). The two agree on its place within a few cm. Right side: the mirror image (photo NASM-SI-2008-5559 shows it there).
